manual_sections: 13.1 阈值标定与置信度校准

calibration_set.source: out-of-fold fused scores of the real samples in the 119-sample competition set (scripts/metrics_common.py, deployed per-fold path)

proxy_source_mix.note: proxy labels derived from L1b features; not human annotation (see reports/stratified_analysis.json for the rule)

calibration_set.independence: THE 119 SAMPLES ARE THE ONLY LABELLED DOMAIN DATA: real scores are out-of-fold but not drawn from an independent pure-real calibration corpus, so every interval below underestimates the true uncertainty of a deployment threshold

high_tier_deployed_rule_fp_budget_2.rule: order statistic admitting at most 2 false positive(s)

high_tier_target_1pct_fp_budget_0.rule: order statistic admitting at most 0 false positive(s)

high_tier_quantile_97pct.rule: empirical 97th percentile (initial estimate only; the manual forbids treating '99th percentile == FPR 1%' as an identity)

low_tier_median.rule: median of the pure-real calibration scores (the deployed thr_low rule)

frozen_deployed_thresholds.note: the value actually shipped in models/fusion.json, derived by evaluate_system.py on the same protocol

absolute_budget_2_deployed_rule.rule: resample the 63 real scores with replacement, recompute the order statistic with a false-positive budget of 2

absolute_budget_0_strict_1pct.rule: resample the 63 real scores with replacement, recompute the order statistic with a false-positive budget of 0

scaled_budget_floor_3pct_of_n.rule: resample the 63 real scores with replacement, recompute the order statistic with a false-positive budget of 1

empirical_fpr_of_frozen_threshold.verdict: 95% CI upper bound above the 3% acceptance level

fraction_of_bootstrap_draws_with_zero_fp.rule: share of resamples of the real calibration scores in which the frozen threshold admits no false positive at all

target_fpr_slope_score_units_per_1pct_fp.sign_convention: negative = a looser (higher) FPR target lowers the threshold
target_fpr_slope_score_units_per_1pct_fp.reading: how far the threshold moves per percentage point of target FPR; a steep slope means the operating point is fragile to FPR re-negotiation, and a large magnitude here means the real-score distribution has a wide gap where the threshold must sit

location_shift.rule: add a constant to every real calibration score, then recompute the threshold (a distribution whose quantiles drift upward/downward)
location_shift.interpretation: the order-statistic threshold tracks a pure location shift one-for-one (drift_ratio ~1); what changes the *false positive count* is the shape, not the shift

scale_change.rule: stretch the real scores around their median by a factor, then recompute the threshold

calibration_set_size.rule: subsample the real calibration scores without replacement and recompute the threshold (how much a smaller calibration set moves it)
calibration_set_size.reading: the threshold spread grows as the calibration set shrinks - the reason the manual asks for a calibration-set size to be reported next to every threshold

repeated_calibration.protocol: 500 random half/half splits of the 63 real scores: the threshold is calibrated on one half and the empirical FPR is measured on the other half (manual 表 13-1 step 6); both halves are out-of-fold scores of real samples

absolute_budget_2.budget_rule: 2 false positives regardless of calibration size (deployed rule)

repeated_calibration.reading: half-size calibration halves have a different real-score composition, so the calibrated threshold moves; the hold-out FPR spread is the honest statement of how well a 3% target transfers. The absolute-budget policy allows 2 false positives on a 31-sample half (6.5%), which is why its hold-out FPR reads higher than the scaled-budget policy - both are reported rather than picking the flattering one.

granularity.note: the 1% guardrail cannot be resolved exactly at this sample size; the 3% acceptance level corresponds to exactly 2 false positives out of 63

limitations: The calibration set is the out-of-fold real scores of the 119 competition samples, not an independent pure-real corpus (none exists in this workspace); bootstrap intervals therefore describe sampling noise within this set only.

Real samples dominate the calibration set with digital/render-like material; the difficult negatives (low light, glare, blur, creases, screenshots) named in manual ch.13.1 are not separately available.
The threshold rule (order statistic with an absolute false-positive budget) is the deployed rule; other rules (e.g. fitting the score distribution) would produce different sensitivities.
